overview.title: 📖 Overview: Guarding the Temple Overnight
overview.subtitle: Tamid 25a–25b
overview.hebrewSource: בִּשְׁלֹשָׁה מְקוֹמוֹת הַכֹּהֲנִים שׁוֹמְרִים בְּבֵית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ
overview.label: The scene:
overview.text: Tractate Tamid opens its Gemara here on 25b, since the Bavli's discussion of this tractate exists only from this point through 33b. The mishna describes the nightly guard duty priests performed in the Temple courtyard, much like guards stationed in a royal palace — a mark of honor for the sacred space. Three chambers served this purpose: Beit Avtinas (where the incense was prepared), Beit HaNitzotz (with its small perpetual fire), and Beit HaMoked (the Hearth, where priests warmed themselves). The mishna details who slept where, how the young priests handled their sacred vestments overnight, and what protocol governed a priest who became ritually impure during the night.

slides.title: 🏛️ Three Places of Nightly Guard Duty
slides.subtitle: Priests stationed like royal guards, in honor of the Temple
rows: Had an upper story — young priests not yet eligible for service kept watch there
Beit HaNitzotz (בֵּית הַנִּיצוֹץ, 'Chamber of the Spark')
Housed a small, perpetual fire used to relight the altar if it went out
Also had an upper story for the young trainee priests
Beit HaMoked (בֵּית הַמּוֹקֵד, 'Chamber of the Hearth')
Held a fire where priests warmed themselves in cold weather
No upper story — a large domed hall on the ground level

slides.title: 🛏️ Inside the Chamber of the Hearth
slides.subtitle: Architecture built for both warmth and rest

steps.content: 1️⃣ The chamber's ceiling was rounded like a cupola (כִּיפָּה) — no upper floor, unlike Avtinas and HaNitzotz
2️⃣ It was a large hall, ringed by rows of stone (רוֹבְדִין) protruding from the walls to serve as benches
3️⃣ The elders of that day's serving priestly patrilineal family slept there overnight
4️⃣ They kept the keys to the Temple courtyard in their own possession while they slept

callout.label: A position of trust:
callout.text: Holding the courtyard keys overnight marked these elders as responsible for the Temple's overall security, distinct from the younger priests' separate sleeping arrangements.

slides.title: 🌙 Who Slept Where, and How
slides.subtitle: Different arrangements for different ranks of priests

boxes.title: Elders of the Serving Family
items: Slept in the Chamber of the Hearth
Held the Temple courtyard's keys overnight

boxes.title: Young Priests Eligible to Serve
items: Also slept in the Chamber of the Hearth
Each on the ground with his own garment, NOT on the stone benches

boxes.title: Young Trainee Priests (not yet eligible)
items: Kept watch in the UPPER stories of Beit Avtinas and Beit HaNitzotz
Separate posts from the main sleeping hall

slides.title: 👕 Never Sleeping in the Sacred Vestments
slides.subtitle: How the eligible young priests handled their garments overnight
slides.hebrewSource: פִּרְחֵי כְהוּנָּה אִישׁ כִּסְתּוֹ בָּאָרֶץ. לֹא הָיוּ יְשֵׁנִים בְּבִגְדֵי קֹדֶשׁ
slides.label: The protocol:
slides.text: The young priests eligible to serve did not sleep on the stone benches, and — critically — they never slept while wearing the sacred priestly vestments. Instead, each removed his sacred garments, folded them, and placed them beneath his own head as a pillow. He then covered himself for warmth with his own personal, non-sacred clothing. This distinction between the sacred vestments (treated with careful respect, never worn casually or during sleep) and personal garments (used freely for practical needs like warmth) reflects the broader halakhic principle that sacred items are reserved strictly for their designated purpose.

slides.title: 🚿 When a Seminal Emission Occurred Overnight
slides.subtitle: The mishna's account begins — and continues into the next daf

nodes.content: 😴 A young priest sleeping in the Chamber of the Hearth experiences a seminal emission, rendering him ritually impure
🚪 He must leave immediately — remaining in the sacred precincts while impure is forbidden
🚶 He 'goes out and walks' — the mishna's account of exactly where he goes and how he purifies himself continues on the following daf

callout.label: Setting up the next daf:
callout.text: This account of the impure priest's nighttime departure route through the Temple complex is the thread the Gemara will pick up next.

summary.principle: The Temple's overnight security rested on a carefully structured system — three guard chambers, distinct sleeping arrangements by rank, sacred vestments strictly separated from personal use during rest, and an immediate, well-defined protocol for any priest who became ritually impure during the night.

flowSteps.content: 🏛️ Three guard chambers: Beit Avtinas, Beit HaNitzotz (both with upper floors for trainees), and Beit HaMoked
🛏️ Beit HaMoked's domed hall: elders slept on stone benches, holding the courtyard's keys
🌙 Young eligible priests slept on the floor, sacred vestments folded beneath their heads

columns.content: 👕 Sacred garments never worn during sleep, only personal clothing used for warmth
🚿 A seminal emission required immediate departure from the sacred space

flowSteps.content: 🎓 Key Principle: honoring the Temple meant precise, rank-based protocols for rest, dress, and departure — nothing left to improvisation

quiz.q: What were the three chambers where priests kept nightly watch in the Temple courtyard, according to the mishna?
o: Beit Avtinas, Beit HaNitzotz, and Beit HaMoked
The Sanctuary, the Holy of Holies, and the Courtyard
The Chamber of Hewn Stone, the Chamber of Salt, and the Chamber of Parva
The Eastern Gate, the Western Gate, and the Nicanor Gate
quiz.e: The mishna names Beit Avtinas (where incense was prepared), Beit HaNitzotz (with its perpetual small fire), and Beit HaMoked (the Hearth, for warmth) as the three guard posts.

quiz.q: What was architecturally distinctive about the Chamber of the Hearth (Beit HaMoked) compared to Beit Avtinas and Beit HaNitzotz?
o: It had two upper stories instead of one
It had no upper story at all — its ceiling was rounded like a cupola, and it was a large hall ringed with stone benches
It was located outside the Temple courtyard entirely
It had no fire at all
quiz.e: Unlike the other two chambers, which had upper floors for young trainee priests, Beit HaMoked was a single large domed hall surrounded by protruding stone benches.

quiz.q: Who slept in the Chamber of the Hearth while holding the keys to the Temple courtyard?
o: The young trainee priests
The elders of the priestly patrilineal family serving that day
The High Priest personally
No one held the keys overnight
quiz.e: The mishna specifies that the elders of the serving priestly family (bet av) slept in the Chamber of the Hearth with the Temple courtyard's keys in their possession.

quiz.q: How did the young priests eligible for service handle their sacred vestments when sleeping in the Chamber of the Hearth?
o: They slept while wearing them for added warmth
They removed and folded them, placing them under their heads as a pillow, and covered themselves with their own personal clothing instead
They hung them on the walls
They left them in Beit Avtinas overnight
quiz.e: The mishna specifies that the young priests never slept in their sacred garments — they removed and folded them for use as a pillow, using their own non-sacred clothes as a blanket.

quiz.q: What happened, according to the mishna, if a young priest experienced a seminal emission while sleeping in the Chamber of the Hearth?
o: He was permitted to remain and simply change his clothes
He had to leave and depart from the sacred space, with the mishna's description of his route continuing into the next daf
He was punished with lashes
Nothing happened; impurity did not apply overnight
quiz.e: The mishna states that such a priest would leave immediately, as ritual impurity requires departure from the sacred precincts — the details of his specific route are picked up in the following daf.
